main_text.p: vuntur[?]. Eodem modo vapores & halitus multi colliguntur in terræ cauernis, ubi condensantur et crassescunt: tandem autem frigido aliquo spiramine interueniente, resoluuntur in tenues guttas sparsim appendentes, quæ temporis progressu continuè coalescunt, atque aquarum copiam efficiunt. Confirmatur hæc sententia aliquot rationibus.

1. Ab experimento in rebus artificialibus, qui ὑ-δραγωγίας[?], id est, aquæductus parare volunt, ita ducunt fossas, ut in eas excipiant aquam e terris defluentem, atque à sublimioribus semper ad inferiores partes decurrentem.

2. Fontes & flumina plurimum ex montibus scaturiunt. Nam & montes plerùq; habet amplas cauernas, in quibus vapores colligi condensariq; compertum est. Quinetiam in ijsdē cauernis ex testudine & lateribus plurima aqua destillat, sæpe etiam aliqua in imo fluit vel consistit. Sunt deniq; montes acri atq; frigori omni ex parte expositi: quamobrem facilè frigus concipiunt, quo vapores condensantur & resoluuntur. Videre autem licet, omnes memorabiles fontes ac fluvios è montibus originem trahere:ut in Germania Rhenus, Danubius, Albis, Mosa, &c.
Porrò multas passim in terra esse cauernas, quales diximus, ex eo cognosci potest, quòd alicubi ampli meatus subterranei & scrobes, atq; in his etiam aqua aliqua consistens inueniuntur: deinde, quòd

page.notes: Running head "AND. HYPERII" set in spaced capitals. Page number "212" is partly worn; the last digit is doubtful. Line 1 begins mid-word ("uuntur") and was read as "vuntur[?]", since the word is cut off at the page top. The Greek word "ὑδραγωγίας" at the line end is doubtful: it is split as "ὑ-" plus a hyphen, and the second line begins with a faint Greek word. Long s is written as plain s. u/v were changed to match the rules (vapores, vel, vuntur). Catchword "non" at lower right. The word "habet" is printed as is, although the sense suggests "habent". The stop and colon in "trahere:ut" are as printed. No headings or notes in the margins.
